title: New Traditional Point & Click Game using AI
author: GhostladyAtMM
selftext:
I've been very busy writing my new point and click adventure game "Mirrors To The Past" and I want to start marketing it, so it gets on the radar.  I still have a long way to go but I'll update as I go along.

\*\*Mirrors To The Past\*\*

A mysterious coastal town. A strange old inn. Curious characters and secrets hiding in unexpected places. This classic point-and-click adventure spans two timelines—1980s America and the Prohibition era of the early 1900s. Explore both eras, solve clever puzzles, uncover hidden secrets, and discover how the past and present are mysteriously connected.  
  
Filled with exploration, mystery, and a little bit of mischief.  
  
I've attached a screenshot of The Strand in Galveston where the protagonist will visit to learn of her grandmother, who was a jazz singer in the early 1900s. The second image is of the old inn, which will be connected to the Tavern, or speakeasy, where her grandmother used to sing. 

I've used all AI to create the images and am using Adventure Game Studio as the game maker. 

Some early gameplay:  [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qEABzq1OV60](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qEABzq1OV60)

comments.author: Original-League-6094
comments.body: Needs some subtle animations on each frame. Like in the first one, you can hear the breeze quite loud, but the palm trees are static. If you just made some very basic blowing animation by just wiggling the top of the trees, it would make the image much more interesting.

replies.author: GhostladyAtMM
replies.body: Thank you for your advice. I plan to add some seagulls flying and if you look at the gaslight it is flickering.  The trees moving is a good point.

comments.author: novokvest
comments.body: Hi! Nice atmospheric visuals! Feels classic. Too bad it does not feature 3rd person protagonist, but it reminds me of Nancy Drew series. I invite you to a small discord [community](https://discord.gg/qza2fVzg8X) of fellow adventure game AI developers to help each other and share.

comments.author: AriaTorres2
comments.body: For the two timelines, are you keeping a shared base layout for locations that appear in both? A few recognizable landmarks could help players spot what changed between eras. I'd also keep anything the player can pick up, or anything you want to animate, separate from the background. That would let you change a clue or add movement without regenerating the whole scene.

replies.author: GhostladyAtMM
replies.body: There will be a trigger which causes a flashback and the room will subtly change and the characters will change.
